reviews.text:
I’ve used Colin irons pool service for my leaks. I have a 10,000 gallon 4ft deep above the ground pool set in the ground.  I got a leak several years ago they came  fixed and I’ve used them ever time o have a leak.
Excellent service and price!!
reviews.author: jan dye

reviews.text: Rick Garrett and the whole team were great work with.  They came out multiple times to do repairs give advice on our existing pool.  We have no leaks and will call them again if we do.
reviews.author: Aaron Evans

reviews.text: They were very responsive and were able to help me quickly resolve a minor issue by using FaceTime and explaining some settings that had to be adjusted. It was greatly appreciated and I will use them again for pool repair; big or small. Thanks!
reviews.author: Ryan Korte

reviews.text: I waited 10 months to provide a review for Colin Irons since I wanted to be convinced of a successful crack repair and resurfacing of my 44 year old pool. All good as far as I’m concerned, Doc and the guys were great and I learned a lot along the way as well. I’ve never dealt with a crack in this pool before and thankfully it is no longer a concern as the pool looks great and the chlorinator installed was a great add. They have earned my recommendation.
reviews.author: Greg H

reviews.text:
The tools this company and its staff stole from my contractor company have still not been returned.

Review of Ryan Nunico and Colin Iron.

*update on previous 1 star review. Colin agrees Ryan works for him, but won’t warranty work because he said it’s a “side job”. Make sure you’re not a “side job” before using Colin Iron or his staff for pool repair.  Colin say’s he doesn’t actually use his own staff to do your work.  He subcontracts all your jobs to other people and they don’t warranty their work. We lost $3,000 to this group and our pool is still leaking. Why not just warranty your work guys?

After leaving my initial review.  Colin told his team of technicians to leave fake reviews in an attempt to bury this review.  Rosevel Contreras is Ryan’s helper and doesn’t own a pool.  He posted that “Colin Iron did work for him” Fake review. Ryan Nunico is the person who won’t warranty the work and doesn’t own a pool.  He says “I recommend Colin for all my pool needs” Fake review.  Are Colin’s reviews all fake?  I wouldn’t trust anything this company has to say.

We are a pool contractor who hired Ryan Nunico based on Colin Iron’s promise that they treat contractors fairly and deliver quality work. Unfortunately, our experience was the complete opposite.

Ryan Nunico claimed he’s been with the company a long time and is Colin’s “best repair guy.” Based on that, we expected professionalism and expertise. Instead, the job was subbed out—without our knowledge—to a third-party crew, essentially kids, who showed up, did sloppy work, and left a mess at our client’s home.

When we asked why the work we gave them was outsourced, their response was essentially, “We can do whatever we want with the work you give us.” That’s completely unacceptable, especially when we’re trusting them with our clients’ homes and our company’s reputation.

Worse, the pool is still leaking two weeks later. We hired two separate, reputable companies to inspect the work, and both confirmed the skimmer Ryan Nunico’s team installed is leaking from the exact same spot. Apparently, instead of replacing the entire skimmer as any qualified professional would, Colin Iron’s team only replaced a section—likely to save time. That kind of shortcut simply doesn’t hold up.

We’ve reached out to Ryan and his team multiple times to give them the opportunity to make this right. They’ve refused to respond.

Save yourself the stress, the damage to your reputation, and the cost of redoing bad work. Don’t use this company. And if you’re relying on older 5-star reviews—be warned: many of those reviewers no longer work with them. After our experience, neither will we.
reviews.author: Justin Rivas

reviews.text:
I have a leak in my pool and called my friend, who’s also a pool builder. He recommended a leak detection company he had used before and said he would help, so he arranged for them to come out. They performed a leak test, which I paid $350 for. They identified an issue, recommended nearly $2,000 in repairs, and I went ahead with the work.

Despite all this, the pool still leaks.

I called my friend to let him know the pool was still leaking, and they reached out to Collins. The company then sent another technician to perform a second leak test after the repairs. When the technician arrived, he told me THEY WOULD ONLY TEST AGAINST THE AREAS THEY HAD REPAIRED. This is an important point to note.
•	What happens if they didn’t identify all the leaks during the first visit?
•	Do they always get it right the first time, or is this a “let’s try this out and see what happens”?

The guy who came out the third time and told me THEY WOULD ONLY TEST AGAINST THE AREAS THEY HAD REPAIRED pointed to an area and said YOU MAY have a leak here but wouldn’t say definitively because THEY WOULD ONLY TEST AGAINST THE AREAS THEY HAD REPAIRED.

There is a lot going on over there—there’s a return and a fountain. They did not offer a solution at all.

The guy left, and I got nothing. So I did the easy thing: I capped the return and capped the fountain lines—and guess what? I still have a leak.

I called my friend again, and he said he would work to get them back out. Eventually, they showed up unannounced. I’m not sure how the communication went between my friend and Collins, but since a significant amount of time had passed—so much so that my pool was already half-empty from the leak—they proceeded to tell me they couldn’t perform a full test under those conditions. They did do a pressure test against the lines and told me there was no leak. So my capping the lines did not make it worse.

And guess what—THEY CHARGED ME AGAIN, even though they had already failed to identify and fix the problem during the first visit, the repairs, and the follow-up visit where they only tested against their previous work.

Now I’m being billed another $350 for a leak test visit, for a problem that was never properly diagnosed from the beginning. After four visits to my property and thousands of dollars, I still have a leaking pool.

Collins will likely reply to this saying there was a breakdown in communication because I went through my friend’s pool company or because I capped the lines myself that they said MAY have a leak.

However, there were several times I TRIED reaching out to them directly, and they told me they couldn’t speak to me because I had gone through my friend’s company. I explained the situation, and MULTIPLE TIMES they said someone would reach out—but no one ever did.

To make matters worse, the concrete work they did as part of the repairs is already showing signs of poor quality—cracking and deteriorating after just a few months. I’m no expert, and maybe this is normal, but I sincerely hope it isn’t.

I really hate the idea of posting a negative review about any company that I know probably does good work for others.

However, that was clearly not my experience.

How many times is a customer expected to pay for a leak test before the company actually finds and fixes the leak? It’s incredibly frustrating and feels like I’m being charged just for them to show up, rather than for any real solution.
reviews.author: David Canington

reviews.text:
I'm so glad that many many years ago I heard about Colin Irons Pool Service. We have used them for big jobs and small ones.   Never have to worry about a job not being done correct the first time.
Thank you very much.
Barb
reviews.author: Nick Kokoron

reviews.text:
Colin Irons did a great job repairing our pool leak, very knowledgeable and professional.
I would highly recommend.
Mike from Southlake, Texas

BLOG FAQ CONTACT US CLIENT LOGIN --> --> --> --> --> --> --> Pool Leak Detection and Repair admin 2025-11-20T22:14:53+00:00 Pool Leak Detection, Repairs & Remodels At Colin Irons Pool Leak Detection and Repairs, we understand that your pool is more than just an investment—it’s a source of joy and relaxation. Entrust your pool leak detection and repair needs to our expert technicians and spend more time enjoying it and less time worrying about leaks. Offering a wide range of pool repair and improvement services for both in-ground and above-ground pools, Colin Irons Pool Leak Detection and Repairs is dedicated to keeping your pool in optimal condition for a stress-free and enjoyable experience. Why Choose Us Our company has been serving pool owners in need of reliable pool repairs and renovations for over 25 years. Frequently Asked Questions How to find a leak in an inflatable pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:31:27+00:00 How to find a leak in an inflatable pool? Look for wet spots under the pool or listen for air hissing if it’s losing air. You can also apply soapy water to the outside —bubbles will form where air or water escapes. For small pinholes, patch kits work well. How to use pool leak detection dye? admin 2025-08-27T15:31:01+00:00 How to use pool leak detection dye? With the pump off, carefully squirt dye near suspected areas (skimmer, returns, cracks). Watch closely—if there’s a leak, the dye will flow toward it. Where do fiberglass pools leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:30:32+00:00 Where do fiberglass pools leak? Fiberglass pools most commonly leak around plumbing penetrations, return jets, skimmers, or fittings . Occasionally, cracks can form in the fiberglass shell itself, though this is less common. Why is my pool level dropping below the skimmer? admin 2025-08-27T15:30:06+00:00 Why is my pool level dropping below the skimmer? If water continues dropping below the skimmer until it stabilizes, the leak is most likely at the return jets, light niche, or pool wall at that level . How does pool leak dye work? admin 2025-08-27T15:29:43+00:00 How does pool leak dye work? The dye is heavier than water and allows you to see the water flowing or traveling to the leak, making it easy to see exactly where water is escaping. It works best when the pump is off, so the water is still. How do I find my pool drain? admin 2025-08-27T15:29:06+00:00 How do I find my pool drain? The main drain is located at the deepest point of your pool’s floor . It may be round or square with a grate cover. Some pools have dual drains for safety. These are used for circulation and not typically to empty the pool. How do I stop my pool from losing water? admin 2025-08-27T15:28:38+00:00 How do I stop my pool from losing water? First, identify the source of the loss. Once located, the leak must be repaired—whether it’s a patch, new plumbing, or resealing a fitting. Keeping up with pool maintenance, balanced chemicals, and timely repairs helps prevent leaks from recurring. How to fix a leak in an inground pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:27:06+00:00 How to fix a leak in an inground pool? Repairs may involve patching cracks with epoxy, replacing failing fittings, or re-plumbing sections of pipe. Because inground pools have complex plumbing systems, professional repair is usually needed for a permanent solution. How to find an underground leak in your pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:26:42+00:00 How to find an underground leak in your pool? This usually requires pressure testing the plumbing lines and using listening and video/vacuum equipment to hear and/or see escaping water underground. Professional services are the best option for underground leaks. How to test for pool leaks? admin 2025-08-27T15:26:13+00:00 How to test for pool leaks? Monitor for loss first: click here for more info: https://colinironspoolservice.com/is-my-pool-leaking/ , then try dye testing for visible leaks. If water loss continues and you can’t find the source, a professional can pressure test your plumbing lines. What can I put in my pool to find a leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:25:30+00:00 What can I put in my pool to find a leak? Leak detection dye (or even food coloring) can be used. Squirt a small amount near suspected leaks, and the dye will be drawn toward the crack or opening. How do I find the source of my pool leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:24:55+00:00 How do I find the source of my pool leak? You can start with dye testing near fittings and lights, but underground plumbing leaks require specialized equipment like pressure testing. A professional leak detection service can locate the spot without unnecessary digging. Does pool evaporation happen at night? admin 2025-08-27T15:23:53+00:00 Does pool evaporation happen at night? Yes. Evaporation happens whenever there’s a difference between the water temperature and the air temperature , even at night. In fact, pools often lose more water overnight if the air is cool and the pool is warm. Is it normal to lose an inch of water a week in a pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:23:28+00:00 Is it normal to lose an inch of water a week in a pool? Yes, losing about an inch of water per week is normal in most climates and is generally caused by evaporation. If your pool loses more than that, it may be a leak. How do I find out where my pool is losing water? admin 2025-08-27T15:23:03+00:00 How do I find out where my pool is losing water? Start with monitoring for loss – Is My Pool Leaking, then carefully check fittings, returns, skimmers, and the pool floor for cracks. If you can’t locate the leak, calling a professional with pressure testing equipment is the fastest and most accurate way. How much water is normal to lose in a pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:21:28+00:00 How much water is normal to lose in a pool? Most pools naturally lose about 1–3 inches per week from evaporation, depending on temperature, humidity, and wind. Anything more is outside the normal range and should be checked for leaks. How often should I have to add water to my pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:20:50+00:00 How often should I have to add water to my pool? In most climates, you’ll need to add water once or twice a week during the swimming season . Adding water more often than that may indicate a leak, especially if your pool is losing more than ½ inch per day. How much does a pool leak cost to fix? admin 2025-08-27T15:20:12+00:00 How much does a pool leak cost to fix? Repair costs vary widely: $200 up to the cost of a full remodel. If you delay finding and fixing the problem, it often costs more in the end. What is the bucket test for a pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:19:34+00:00 What is the bucket test for a pool? The bucket test is a simple way to confirm if water loss is from evaporation or a leak . By comparing evaporation in a bucket to that in your pool, you can determine if water loss is abnormal. If the pool water drops more than the bucket water, it may be leaking. Why did my pool lose water overnight? admin 2025-08-27T15:18:57+00:00 Why did my pool lose water overnight? Sudden, significant water loss overnight is often due to a major leak in the plumbing system or a large liner tear . It can also happen if the pump was running and forced water through a failing pipe or seal. Rapid overnight drops usually require immediate professional leak detection. How to find a leak in a pool without equipment? admin 2025-08-27T15:18:22+00:00 How to find a leak in a pool without equipment? Inspect the liner or shell carefully for cracks, feel for soft spots on the floor, and perform the bucket test . You can also use a few drops of food coloring or dye around suspect areas like the skimmer or returns—the dye will flow toward the leak if there is one. What is the most common cause of a pool leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:17:43+00:00 What is the most common cause of a pool leak? The most common causes are structural cracks, failing seals around fittings, and damaged underground plumbing lines . Vinyl liners can also develop pinholes or tears over time. Most leaks occur at points where different materials meet—such as the skimmer throat, return fittings, or light niches. How to detect a pool leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:17:21+00:00 How to detect a pool leak? Start with a bucket test to rule out evaporation, then move on to dye testing around fittings, lights, and seams to see if water is being pulled through a crack. For underground or hard-to-find leaks, professionals can sometimes use pressure testing and listening devices to locate the problem. How do you distinguish evaporation from leaks? admin 2025-08-27T15:16:52+00:00 How do you distinguish evaporation from leaks? Beyond the bucket test, consider the rate of loss . Normal evaporation rarely exceeds ½ inch per day, even in hot climates. If your pool loses more, or if the water stops dropping once it reaches a certain point (like below the skimmer or return fittings), that’s a strong sign of a leak rather than natural evaporation. Why is my pool losing water below the skimmer? admin 2025-08-27T15:16:15+00:00 Why is my pool losing water below the skimmer? If the water level drops consistently below the skimmer and then stops, this usually indicates a leak in the pool structure or plumbing at that depth . Common culprits include return jets, light niches, or cracks in the wall below the skimmer. How to fix a leak in a pool? admin 2025-08-27T15:15:19+00:00 How to fix a leak in a pool? The fix depends on the leak’s source. Small liner tears can be repaired with a vinyl patch kit , while cracks in concrete or gunite pools may be sealed with epoxy or resurfacing material. Plumbing leaks often require pressure testing and pipe replacement . For best results, a professional leak detection service can identify the issue and provide a long-term solution rather than a temporary fix. How to tell if a pool is leaking or evaporating? admin 2025-08-27T15:14:41+00:00 How to tell if a pool is leaking or evaporating? The easiest way is to perform the bucket test . Fill a bucket with pool water, set it on a pool step, and mark the water levels on both the bucket and the pool wall. After 24 hours, compare the two. If the pool’s water level drops more than the bucket’s, you likely have a leak. Evaporation will affect both equally, while leaks will only affect the pool. We recommend that you turn off water features during this test. For further monitoring, click here for more info . How much water should a pool lose in a week? admin 2025-08-27T15:13:33+00:00 How much water should a pool lose in a week? Under normal conditions, most pools lose about ¼ to ½ inch of water per day , which adds up to around 1 to 3 inches per week . The exact amount depends on the climate, wind, sun exposure, and whether your pool is heated. Anything beyond this range is usually a sign of a leak or excessive splash-out from swimming activity. Where does water go when a pool leaks? admin 2025-08-27T15:12:57+00:00 Where does water go when a pool leaks? When a pool leaks, the water usually seeps into the ground or soil surrounding the pool. Depending on where the leak is located, it might also flow along the outside of underground plumbing lines, causing soil erosion or even making its way into nearby structures. In some cases, leaks can lead to wet spots in your yard or cause your pool deck to shift or crack over time. Why is my pool losing 1 inch of water a day? admin 2025-08-27T15:12:10+00:00 Why is my pool losing 1 inch of water a day? Losing 1 inch of water per day is typically too much to be evaporation alone, especially if weather conditions are mild. This rate usually points to a leak somewhere in the system—whether in the pool structure, plumbing, or equipment pad. A small leak can waste hundreds of gallons daily and increase your water bill, so it’s important to rule out evaporation. Click here for more info and schedule a professional inspection if the water loss continues. Where is the most common place for a pool leak? admin 2025-08-27T15:11:10+00:00 Where is the most common place for a pool leak? The most common places for pool leaks are around the skimmer, return fittings, main drain, and underground plumbing lines . Skimmer leaks happen often because of the stress between the concrete pool and the plastic skimmer throat. Plumbing lines are also prone to leaks due to ground movement or wear and tear over time. In vinyl pools, small tears in the liner are a frequent culprit. Can I Turn Off My Skimmers and Still Run My Pool/Spa? admin 2023-12-12T15:28:18+00:00 Can I Turn Off My Skimmers and Still Run My Pool/Spa? Yes, it is possible to run your pool or spa with your skimmers turned off. However, running your equipment on your main drains alone will allow surface debris to accumulate in your pool or spa. Keep in mind that your pump and pool equipment needs to have at least one other method of suction open and operating if you close off the skimmers. If the water in your pool is too low to fill the skimmer basket, there is a simple way to run your pool on the main drain alone. Close the skimmer valves at your equipment pad. Make certain the valve for your pool main drains is open. Do not run your pool with all suction valves closed off at the same time. Running your pool or spa on your main drains alone is useful in a few situations. For instance, if you are leaving town for an extended period and are unable to monitor your pool daily, running your equipment’s suction on the main drains alone is an easy precaution. Using only the main drains is also an alternative if your leak is causing the pool to drain below the skimmers. Running your skimmers without enough water could cause damage to your pool’s pump. However, as long as your skimmers are not drawing or sucking air, they can be used. How Can I Identify the Skimmer Valve at My Equipment? admin 2023-08-28T23:22:50+00:00 How Can I Identify the Skimmer Valve at My Equipment? Locate your pool’s pump at the equipment pad. Protruding out of the front of your pump will be a PVC manifold that controls the suction of your pool. The suction manifold of a pool consists of pool main drains, spa main drains, and skimmers. They are responsible for directing water from your pool or spa back to your equipment for filtration. The suction manifold should include valves that will allow you to control which specific pipes of your pool’s suction are turned on or off. One or more of these pipes will control your skimmers. To identify the pipes that run to your skimmers, your pool pump must be running. Once your pump is primed and running properly, try turning each separate suction valve on and off, one at a time. If the suction at the bottom of your skimmer body stops, the valve to that skimmer is closed. To confirm this pipe and valve run to this specific skimmer, open the valve. If your skimmer resumes suction you have identified the valve correctly. Never run your pump with all the valves closed. If you have any questions and/or would like to schedule our services, please contact us at 940-484-4468 or click here to contact us. We are here for you! How Do I Know if My Skimmer is Working? admin 2023-12-12T15:27:19+00:00 How Do I Know if My Skimmer is Working? Pool skimmers are essential to keep circulation and filtration in your pool or spa, and ensure your water is clean and clear. The function of a skimmer is to remove floating dirt and debris that may accumulate in your pool and spa. Without properly functioning skimmers, your pool or spa water will accumulate unwanted surface debris. Your skimmer includes a basket that captures leaves, tree branches, and larger unwanted objects from being pulled through your pool’s pipes, which could cause damage and blockage to your equipment. Please check the basket for any holes or cracks that could allow debris to get past the skimmer and into the pump. Identifying if your skimmer is working is simple. Most importantly, begin with ensuring that your pool water is at the correct level of full (e.g. To the middle of the tile line or just below the bottom of the overflow grate). Once you have corrected or verified the proper water level, turn on the pump at the equipment pad. Wait for your pump to fully prime. Open your skimmer valve(s). At your pool, the bottom of your skimmer body should be sucking water and debris down its pipe. If you can see and feel the water and debris being pulled down your skimmer’s body, your skimmer is working correctly. If no suction is happening, your skimmer may have a break or blockage. If your skimmer suction seems weak, you may need to clean the filter at your equipment pad. A dirty filter will cause your pool’s suction to reduce in intensity and effectiveness. Call us for advice on troubleshooting low or high pressure on your filter. 940-484-4468. When feeling your skimmers for suction, be cautious of inserting your hand in or around the skimmer pipe. Strong suction could cause your hand to get caught in the pipe. An alternative approach is to watch any floating dirt or debris to see if the suction pulls it down the skimmer pipe. If you have any questions and/or would like to schedule our services, please contact us at 940-484-4468 or click here to contact us. We are here for you! What is a Dive and Dye Test? admin 2023-08-28T23:06:27+00:00 What is a Dive and Dye Test? One approach to detecting leaks in a pool or spa is known as a Dive and Dye Test. Using a small syringe with colored dye, our Diving Technician searches throughout and around the shell of the pool, for any cracks or holes that may be causing your leak. Read more about our dive and dye test . If you have any questions and/or would like to schedule our services, please contact us at 940-484-4468 or click here to contact us. We are here for you! What is a Pressure Test? admin 2023-12-12T15:29:06+00:00 What is a Pressure Test? One key phase of leak detection is the plumbing pressure test. During a pressure test, our Technicians test the pool’s equipment and plumbing for leaks caused by breaks or cracks in the PVC pipes used to plumb your pool or spa. If you are experiencing rapid drops in water levels, you likely have a broken pipe underground. A water loss of approximately 2-3 inches every 24 hours often indicates a plumbing leak, as opposed to a structural leak such as a crack in the gunite. You can read more about this test in our blog entry about pressure tests . If you have any questions and/or would like to schedule our services, please contact us at 940-484-4468 or click here to contact us. We are here for you!
